clue.text: Rule out report of how lazy compiler acquired crossword?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the phrase that follows is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: a lazy setter might get a puzzle already written, with its clues done beforehand

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a rumour that an idle setter bought in a finished puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: PRE-CLUED, clued in advance, says the same as PRECLUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude something is to make it impossible, so prevent or exclude it in advance.

clue.text: Standard jeans – slim gent seeking every other option

indicators.note: every other means taking only the alternate items in a sequence

blocks.note: the even-placed letters of these words

explanation.surface: A slim man in regular jeans browses for other clothing choices.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a flag, especially one flown by a ship, and a standard is also a flag.

clue.text: New in cricket side, needing time before hard stretch

indicators.note: in places the first-named piece inside the next one
before puts the following pieces after the earlier ones in order

blocks.note: leg side is one half of a cricket field, the on side
N is the abbreviation for new
T is the abbreviation for time
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A newcomer to a cricket team needs time before a tough spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A length is an extent or expanse, and so a stretch, of road, time or cloth.

clue.text: Detectives given instruction to arrest Republican in a state

indicators.note: arresting someone means seizing and holding them, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: DIs are detective inspectors
someone given instruction has been taught
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Police officers learn how to arrest a party member in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' looks like geography, but it means emotionally agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a state is very upset and agitated, which is what distraught means.

clue.text: Carve hearts and so on at the front

indicators.note: at the front places the second-named piece ahead of the first in the answer

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation of et cetera
H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A carver of initials adds hearts and other doodles to the front of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut a design into a surface such as metal or glass, a kind of engraving.

clue.text: Pathetic meeting ...

blocks.note: first meaning: arousing pity or tender feeling
second meaning: in physical contact with

explanation.walkthrough: Pathetic is used in its older sense of moving rather than useless; the ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means emotionally moving, and also describes surfaces in contact with one another.

clue.text: ... postpone or carry on?

definitions.note: a noun here: something carried on from an earlier time

blocks.note: first meaning: defer to a later date
second meaning: a thing or person kept on from a previous period

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the previous clue, suggesting a meeting being put off.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold over is to delay a decision; a holdover is a survivor retained from earlier times.

clue.text: Sanctimonious, having a tendency to scoff about Right

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed round the other

blocks.note: to scoff is to eat greedily, like a pig
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A self-righteous person mocks the political right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' looks like jeering, but in British slang it means to gobble food.
explanation.definitionFit: Priggish describes a smug person who behaves as though morally superior to others.

clue.text: Trade in vehicle I parked by headland

indicators.note: something parked by another sits right next to it, so the pieces stand side by side

blocks.note: a bus is a vehicle
taken as written
a ness is a promontory, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A trader parks a vehicle on a coastal cape to sell their goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Business means commerce, the buying and selling of goods, just as trade does.

clue.text: Reckoning to have bowled poorly

blocks.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
poorly is a British word for unwell

explanation.surface: A cricketer judges that they bowled badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is an account of money owed, and an old sense of reckoning is exactly that.

clue.text: More than one central part in clue to be solved

indicators.note: a puzzle to be solved must be worked out, so these letters still need sorting into order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A solver hunts for the key element hidden in an unsolved clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclei is the plural of nucleus, the core or central part of an atom or cell, hence 'more than one'.

clue.text: They'll get pipes going in lake – with people having a row that should be lead-free

indicators.note: being free of its lead means the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
people in a row, a quarrel, are fighters

explanation.surface: Pipe-smokers squabble by a lake, while someone mutters about unleaded fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with cow here, a quarrel, not a line or a boating trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighters are small devices that produce a flame, used by smokers to light pipes and cigarettes.

clue.text: Pack skimpy underwear as clothing for run

indicators.note: clothing wraps around a body, so one piece is dressed around another

blocks.note: a thong is minimal underwear
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A jogger stuffs scanty underwear into a bag for going running.
explanation.definitionFit: A throng is a crowd of people pressed together, as is a pack of fans.

clue.text: Humanitarian's trial is cut – that's corrupt

indicators.note: something corrupt has been spoiled and twisted, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An aid worker's court case is shortened, a sign of a crooked process.
explanation.definitionFit: Altruistic describes selfless concern for others' wellbeing, a charitable, philanthropic outlook.

clue.text: Change of lens unless needed for moody feeling

indicators.note: a change rearranges something, so the letters following are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumpy photographer insists on switching lenses before cheering up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sullenness is a sulky, gloomy bad temper, the state of being in a mood.

clue.text: Weak are more unco-operative

definitions.note: a verb phrase read cryptically as two words, help less

blocks.note: first meaning: powerless, unable to act
second meaning, read cryptically: to give others less assistance

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: split the answer into two words and it describes doing less to assist.
explanation.definitionFit: Helpless means lacking strength or the power to defend oneself, so feeble.

clue.text: Left wing's first half getting stuck into passing and tackle

indicators.note: keeping only the first half of a word drops its later letters
something stuck into another is lodged inside it

blocks.note: passing is a euphemism for dying
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football winger gets stuck in to a pass and makes a tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture is false: passing is death, not a ball moved between players.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a problem is to handle or address it, an informal synonym phrase.

clue.text: Lunatic orating about year for revolution

indicators.note: a lunatic is crazy, so the following letters are scrambled madly
about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A deranged speaker holds forth for a year about overthrowing the state.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolution suggests political uprising, but here it means spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyration is circular motion around an axis, and a revolution is one full turn.

clue.text: High and low will be present, after really going in opposite directions

indicators.note: going in places one piece inside the pair of letters that surround it
after places the first-named piece at the end, behind the rest

blocks.note: east and west are opposite compass points
really and very are both intensifiers
to be present is to be here

explanation.surface: Someone promises to turn up after setting off every which way.
explanation.definitionFit: To search high and low is to look in all places, which is the sense of the idiom.

clue.text: One murdering great joke?

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who takes life
second meaning: a hilarious gag, informally

explanation.walkthrough: Together it reads as a dark joke about a murderer; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an assassin, and informally anything outstanding, such as a gag that makes people die laughing.

clue.text: Make 'Raking Fire' part of surrealist RA festival

indicators.note: part of means only a section of the words that follow is wanted

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An artwork titled Raking Fire is shown at a Royal Academy surrealist festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks dress the definition as an art title; RA is the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack with machine-gun fire from low-flying aircraft, sweeping across targets.

clue.text: Hurry along or up in bike race

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top
in places the reversed piece inside the other one

blocks.note: taken as written
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A rider hurries along or uphill during a cycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: To trot is to move at a brisk pace between walking and running.

clue.text: Column goes into reversing lateral liposuction

indicators.note: the answer goes into the words that follow, so it sits inside them
reversing means the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A newspaper column covers side-on fat removal surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar is an upright supporting post in a building, which is what an architectural column is.

clue.text: Disturbing someone in hospital, ringing in

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: in Britain a sister is a senior nurse on a ward
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worrying figure lurks on a hospital ward, phoning in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Someone in hospital' suggests a patient, but it is the nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister describes something that gives a threatening, ominous impression, so it is unsettling.

clue.text: Anger surrounds team backing pick-me-up

indicators.note: surrounds puts one piece around the other
backing means going backwards, so the combined letters are read right to left

blocks.note: to rile is to anger
a cricket or football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A furious fan's mood is lifted by the team going into reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a magical or medicinal potion thought to restore vigour, so a tonic.

clue.text: Loyalist beginning to pen criminal law

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so one piece is shut up inside the other
criminal suggests something crooked, so the word that follows is bent out of shape

blocks.note: a start is a beginning
taken as written

explanation.surface: A faithful supporter starts drafting a law about crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart is a dependable, devoted supporter of a party or cause.

clue.text: Rear deer

blocks.note: first meaning: at the back
second meaning: a female red deer

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it looks like a farmer raising deer, with rear as a verb; it is really the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adjective for the back part of an animal and as a noun for a female red deer.

clue.text: Most unusual, Conservative's interrupting converted actress

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle, so one piece goes inside another
converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tory politician heckles an actress who has changed her religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcest is the superlative of scarce, meaning most rare or hardest to find.
